correctness.rationale: Exact algebra yields mass h(s), composition f(s), and the discounted logarithmic edge deficit. Uniform convergence supplies the boundary. At s=0, f(s)=λs(1+O(s)), g(s)=λs+O(s²). For λ<2 the normalized sum is dominated by (Λ/2)^j and the post-exit tail is o(s), giving λ/(2−λ). For λ=2 an exit at N=log_2(1/s)+O(1) has N terms each s(1+O(δ)), giving 1/log2. For λ>2 g is globally positive and pre-/post-exit sums lie between positive multiples of 2^{−N}≈s^α. Swap a,b for the other endpoint; the mass deficit follows by exponentiation. Fractional exact arithmetic and decimal spot checks pass, but are not substitutes for these proofs.

originality.rationale: The two closest published exact-radial-graph results are explicitly identified and credited: neither records the boundary-vertex asymptotic rate. The full originating manuscript establishes existence and interior-saddle tangent only. The present three-phase endpoint regularity classification requires separate first-exit analysis, proving exact slope, logarithmic resonance coefficient, and sharp fractional exponent; neither an existing formula alone nor projective convergence states those asymptotics. General invariant-manifold theory and unindexed equivalents remain priority risks.
residual_risks: Exact global radial product is prior mathematics; edge rates may be derivable using known invariant-manifold asymptotic techniques not indexed under these search terms.
